executiveSummary.title: WHAT THE DATA SAYS
executiveSummary.narrative:
Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared in at least one AI answer for 45% of the traveler needs we tested, showing that AI recognizes the hotel as relevant across a broad range of stays. Across every individual AI answer, however, Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared 26.9% of the time. In practical terms, the hotel fits many of the searches being made, but a traveler will not consistently see Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel in the hotel options surfaced.

Leisure Travel is Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's clearest competitive strength. The hotel appeared in 29.7% of AI answers for these searches, compared with 7.8% for the comparable hotels used in this analysis — about 3.8 times as often as the comparable hotels used in this analysis. Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel appeared in the Top 3 60.6% of the time, showing how prominently it is positioned when AI includes it.

The main opportunity is consistency: the hotel is already relevant across many traveler needs, so the next focus is understanding where it is absent from individual AI results. No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet, so change over time is not shown.

sections.headline: Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's most important issue is concentrated competitive displacement by New York Marriott Marquis, not a vague visibility problem.
sections.keyInsight: New York Marriott Marquis appears in 28 monitored scenarios where Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel is absent. That concentration matters more than a long competitor list because it identifies a repeatable substitution pattern. Related Reality Gap pressure includes Full-Service Hotel at 2.3% recognition, which may help explain why the hotel is not carried into those answers.
sections.whyItMatters: Leadership needs to understand why specific alternatives are surfaced instead of Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel in recurring demand contexts. Otherwise attention may stay on average scores while missing the concentrated leak. A displacement pattern that repeats is more actionable than a soft overall visibility narrative.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on the demand contexts where New York Marriott Marquis is consistently surfaced instead of Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel. Determine whether the relevant attributes and use cases are clearly represented across priority sources, and whether the hotel's own proposition is complete for those same contexts.
sections.whatToReview: Open the underlying displacement evidence for New York Marriott Marquis and compare attributes cited in those answers with Renaissance New York Times Square Hotel's first-party and major travel-source representation. Confirm whether the same cues appear when the hotel is present.
